claim.why_it_matters: The ten items at the top of page 27 are indented one level deeper in the PDF than "The following intrinsic functions were added or enhanced:" — they are the continuation of the "The following were general enhancements:" sub-list opened on page 26, which page 26's markdown does nest correctly. Page 27 flattens them to column zero, making them siblings of the two group headings instead of members of the general-enhancements group. The items themselves are all present, in the right order, with the right wording, so nothing normative is lost; this is a list-nesting break across a page boundary in the non-normative Foreword. Reported for completeness only — lowest priority in this batch.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed by pixel measurement of the 300dpi renders of pages 26 and 27, not by eyeballing. Page 27 (spec_p27.png, 2550x3300) has exactly three left-edge columns in the list region: x=334/336 for ordinary body text (the closing 'Any feedback or questions...' paragraph), x=409 for a first-level bullet, x=482 for a second-level bullet. The ten items 'Inline exception handling...' through 'Type declarations may now be external items' every one measure left=482 (their wrapped continuation lines measure 535-537, i.e. hanging-indented under the 482 dash). The two group headings 'The following intrinsic functions were added or enhanced:' (y=1126) and 'Additional compiler directives were added:' (y=1706) both measure left=409. Their own sub-items (BASECONVERT..TRIM, COBOL-WORDS..REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH) measure left=482 — identical to the ten items above. So in the PDF the ten items sit at the SAME depth as BASECONVERT, one level DEEPER than the two headings. Cross-checked page 26 (spec_p26.png), which has a slightly different left margin (verso/recto): body text left=266, '— The following were general enhancements:' left=340, and its nine listed sub-items left=413. The offsets from body text are identical on both pages (+74/+75 for level 1, +147/+148 for level 2), so the ten items on page 27 are demonstrably a continuation of page 26's general-enhancements sub-list, exactly as claimed. Checked the real transcription in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, not just the extracted work unit: page 26 uses genuine markdown list syntax ('- — The following were general enhancements:' with '  - — ...' children), while page 27 renders the ten items as bare column-zero em-dash lines, with '— The following intrinsic functions were added or enhanced:' also at column zero and only its children indented four spaces. The flattening is therefore real and visible within page 27's own text: the markdown makes the ten items siblings of the two headings when the PDF makes them children of a heading on the previous page. Refutation attempts all failed: the text is not merely reflowed or hyphenated (all ten items are present verbatim, in order, at the wrong depth); this is not page-break furniture (the depth difference is measurable against two same-page reference columns, independent of the page boundary); the claim misquotes neither source. Meaning impact is nil — this is the non-normative Foreword's 'main changes' list, no normative requirement or general rule depends on the grouping. Severity 'cosmetic' is correct.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described, with two additions for the fixer. (1) The mis-nesting is verifiable within page 27 alone — it does not require the page-26 context to detect — because the ten items measure left=482, identical to the BASECONVERT..TRIM sub-items further down the same page, while the two group headings measure left=409. (2) The two pages also disagree on transcription STYLE, which is the likely root cause: page 26 encodes the list with real markdown bullets ('- — heading' / '  - — child'), whereas page 27 encodes it as literal em-dash text lines with four-space indentation for children and none for parents. A fix should indent the ten items to the child level and, ideally, normalize page 27 to page 26's markdown-list style so the sub-list rejoins its parent across the page break.
